summary: This bill requires the Secretaries of State and Homeland Security and the Attorney General to deny all visas and immigration benefits to any alien who adheres to Sharia law, revoke benefits and remove such aliens already in the United States, and bars judicial review of those decisions.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority. It focuses exclusively on immigration eligibility criteria and enforcement mechanisms.
No tax-related provisions appear in the bill text.
The legislation does not address healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill directly amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to bar admission, visas, and immigration benefits for any alien who adheres to Sharia law. It mandates revocation of status and removal for those already in the United States, plus penalties for nondisclosure. This constitutes a significant new restriction on immigration pathways and strengthens border/enforcement controls.
No content related to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill does not involve defense spending, military policy, or national security appropriations.
No environmental or climate provisions are present.
The legislation makes no changes to welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety-net policies.
No education policy, school funding, or choice provisions exist.
The bill does not address controlled substances, decriminalization, or drug enforcement.
While the bill expands removal authority, it operates entirely within immigration law rather than criminal sentencing, policing, or rehabilitation frameworks.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization measures are included.
The bill has no fiscal or debt-related implications.
No provisions concerning LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
Foreign aid is not mentioned or affected.
The legislation contains nothing related to voting access or election procedures.
No technology regulation, data privacy, or surveillance provisions appear.
Worker protections, union rights, and employment policy are absent.

The bill imposes an immigration bar based on adherence to a specific religious legal system (Sharia). While this touches on religion, it does not engage the domestic civil-rights-versus-religious-exemption framework described by the topic.
